withheld.headline: Namhae bamboo weirs elevate Korea’s anchovies to premium delicacy
withheld.evidence: Anchovies are indispensable when boiling soup and making kimchi. They are a common ingredient on Korean tables, but the top grade can sell for hundreds of thousands of won per kilogram at department stores during the holidays. This is the story of "jukbang anchovies" caught in the Jizok Strait in Namhae, South Gyeongsang. The secret to their higher price, despite being the same anchovies, lies in how they are caught. Instead of hauling them up in nets all at once, they are taken using the powerful current and bamboo weirs, a 500-year-old fishing method. Jukbang anchovies are those caught by the "jukbangryeom" method in the Jizok Strait between Samdong-myeon and Changseon-myeon in Namhae County, South Gyeongsang. Jukbangryeom is a traditional fish trap made by driving oak stakes about 10 meters long into the seabed and weaving bamboo screens between them to form a V shape. They head out by boat at ebb tide, open the baltong gate, go in, and first remove trash, starfish, and jellyfish. Ordinary anchovies easily get injured and lose scales as they snag in nets or tangle with other fish. Because the tiny bones are eaten whole, various nutrients can be consumed together. They are versatile for stir-fries and broth, as well as jeotgal, jjigae, and hoe-muchim.

withheld.headline: Hurricane Isaias downgraded after making landfall in Florida
withheld.evidence: Hurricane Isaias, the first of the 2026 Atlantic season, made landfall Friday night along the northern Gulf Coast of Florida, bringing with it heavy rains, powerful winds and the risk of life-threatening flash flooding and storm surges. Isaias is continuing north across the Southeastern United States after being downgrade from a hurricane to a post-tropical cyclone, the BBC's US partner CBS News reports . Florida, Alabama, and Georgia have each issued states of emergency amid warnings of life-threatening storm surge that could cause up to 9 feet (2.7m) of flooding in some areas. Isaias is one of three storm systems affecting North America this weekend, with the two others hitting Mexico and Southern California in the El-Niño fuelled warm waters of the Pacific Ocean. Both Florida and Alabama instituted mandatory evacuations to thousands of people due to the storm. In Florida, those evacuations include coastal communities in direct aim of the powerful storm. Florida Senator Rick Scott encouraged residents in designated areas to evacuate as soon as possible, as he warned in a social media post: "DO NOT WAIT! Get out NOW!" Hurricane Isaias is the first hurricane in the Atlantic's hurricane season, which largely has been delayed due to El Niño conditions in the Pacific. It marks the first time in more than 30 years that a hurricane did not form till October. withheld.headline: Putin tells Trump peace talks are unlikely, cites Ukraine drone attacks
withheld.evidence: Negotiators aim to present a proposal to Russia in the coming weeks, meanwhile Putin says resumption of talks unlikely. Russian President Vladimir Putin has said an immediate resumption of peace talks with Ukraine is unlikely, citing drone attacks on Moscow during parliamentary elections last month. In a phone call with US President Donald Trump on Friday, Putin said Moscow was ready to resume negotiations with Kyiv after the parliamentary elections. However, the drone attacks on the capital made the resumption of trilateral peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US unlikely. “By launching a large-scale drone attack on Moscow, other cities and polling stations on the most important day of the elections, and by targeting some people involved in organising the elections, the Kyiv regime has, in reality, interrupted the possibility of an immediate resumption of the negotiation process,” said Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov about the call with Trump. “As the president said, we will now assess when these negotiations can resume,” he added regarding the trilateral talks. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Thursday that Russia’s war in Ukraine is at a dangerous stalemate and the United States will keep working towards a deal to end the war. “All that money goes toward the war against people, against Ukraine, against all of us. I believe our team is simply being used as a smokescreen. And that is certainly not fair,” he said in a statement. In response to the US-Russia diesel deal, a government spokesperson said the United Kingdom would continue to “maintain pressure on Russia through the toughest sanctions regime ever imposed by the UK.”

withheld.headline: Syrian army takes control of al-Shaddadi base after coordination with U.S.
withheld.evidence: The Syrian Army has assumed control of the al-Shaddadi military base in northeastern Syria’s Hasakah province, following coordination with U.S. officials, according to the Syrian Defense Ministry’s media department. In a statement carried by Syrian Arab News Agency, the ministry said the base was formally handed over after arrangements were completed with U.S. authorities. Syrian army units have since moved to secure the facility and its surrounding perimeter. The transfer comes just days after Damascus announced it had taken control of the al-Tanf military base in southeastern Syria. On February 12, the Defense Ministry said the handover of al-Tanf followed direct coordination between Syrian and American officials, marking a significant shift in the military presence in the area. United States Central Command (CENTCOM) confirmed its withdrawal from al-Tanf after nearly a decade of operations there. In a statement, CENTCOM said U.S. forces remain prepared to respond to any potential threats from ISIS and will continue supporting partner-led efforts aimed at preventing the group’s resurgence in the region.
